routes.E: Scoped agent-supplied fact or domain check
routes.D: Deferred, outside current scope, or source-specific

families.identity: Entity, session, operation and authority identity

evidenceRoles.extension: Candidate semantic fact for a present mechanism; admission/invalidation still needed
evidenceRoles.consumer: Fact needs an additional enforcement/protocol consumer
evidenceRoles.app-check: Domain/prediction check, not an optimization certificate
evidenceRoles.ordinary: Primarily reusable checking or authored code work
evidenceRoles.deferred: Evidence transfer depends on a deferred/source-specific feature

items.claim: Call atomicity and commit-delayed channel sends.
items.current: PG transactions can be authored; Endpoints invokes the handler without wrapping it in a transaction or delaying arbitrary external effects.
items.failure: First SQL statement commits; second throws. Or an email is sent before a later SQL rollback.
items.agent: Trace an unsupported adapter to establish existing transaction participation and post-commit behavior. If those behaviors are absent, change app/adapter code; evidence cannot create atomicity.

items.claim: Foreign-call effect/tier declarations, with separate transactional hook obligations.
items.current: Supported SQL has summaries. There is no general agent-evidence admission format or hook runtime.
items.failure: An HTTP helper writes shopping items although the visible SQL only updates recipes.
items.agent: Inspect exact implementation, hooks, configuration, failure paths and database binding; supply a scoped read/write bound. Hook ordering remains a distinct claim, as in L5b.

items.claim: Invalidate queries sharing affected entities.
items.current: Registered read/write footprints are intersected; unknown bounds refetch. SQL-only fallback can omit imported-call effects, so complete handler coverage is conditional.
items.failure: A helper writes tags, but tags are absent from the emitted write set, so a retained tag query is skipped.
items.agent: Supply missing upper bounds for opaque calls, including failures and indirect writes. The compiler unions these with SQL. Conditional precision is optional; a complete unconditional bound is useful.

items.claim: One logical snapshot per query and a restricted deterministic query context.
items.current: A single SQL statement uses PG semantics. Multiple handler statements and parallel endpoint reads are not enclosed in a shared snapshot; external calls remain allowed.
items.failure: A query reads a total, another commit occurs, then it reads the component rows from a different snapshot.
items.agent: Inspect hidden read dependencies and nondeterminism. To guarantee a shared snapshot, authored transactions with suitable isolation or new runtime behavior must exist.

items.claim: Atomic mutation execution, distinct from external actions and their retry constraints.
items.current: Handlers run once per dispatched request; reads retry. Atomicity of handler writes depends on authored SQL/transactions.
items.failure: An external charge succeeds and a later database write fails; rerunning the handler charges twice.
items.agent: Certify an existing transaction participant, a particular no-effect failure prefix, or a deduplication contract separately. None implies the other two.

items.claim: Fragment masking restricts component data access.
items.current: Endpoint collections expose their row schema; no Relay-style fragment ownership/witness API is provided.
items.failure: A component reads a field it never declared because the shared collection happens to contain it.
items.agent: No evidence fact can install masking. An agent could implement a chosen interface/compiler feature; it is a separate product feature, not needed for current refetch coherence.

items.claim: Optimistic merging/rollback with authored update and invalidation semantics.
items.current: DB transactions and Endpoints settlement manage overlays; supported relation models propagate optimism. Arbitrary app predictions are not validated automatically.
items.failure: A title is trimmed on the server but raw optimistic input remains untrimmed, or changing a field moves a row across a filter.
items.agent: Provide domain generators and an explicit comparison law for real onMutate/server executions. A test can expose a wrong prediction; legitimate server-state divergence remains allowed.

items.claim: Client/server divergence settles through authority; source engines also replay/rebase.
items.current: Endpoints replaces guesses with authoritative reads and handles overlapping responses conservatively. Durable offline replay/rebase is not provided.
items.failure: Two users reserve the last item; both predict success but only one server operation succeeds.
items.agent: Test authored conflict policy and prediction under declared initial-state assumptions. Framework settlement needs its own history oracle; passing app tests does not install a sync engine.

items.claim: PG batch rollback excludes arbitrary remote operations.
items.current: A handler may use a PG transaction; refresh also reconciles partial writes after a throw. There is no distributed rollback mechanism.
items.failure: A transaction rolls back recipes while a remote shopping service has already committed its changes.
items.agent: Document participants and completion boundaries; inspect existing compensation if any. Repair code/semantics when the desired atomicity is not implemented.

items.claim: Configured row/column and expression-based permissions are enforced.
items.current: Endpoint handlers retain authored authorization. The framework validates input and collection descriptors but does not supply application permission rules.
items.failure: A signed-in user submits another user’s row ID to an update guarded only by a login check.
items.agent: Trace an opaque authorization helper and all accepting paths against an authored policy. An agent can repair code; evidence describes enforcement already present, not policy intent.

items.claim: Complete sync checkpoints and matching write arrival before optimism retires.
items.current: Endpoints uses request closure plus authoritative reads, not sync checkpoints or operation-tagged change delivery.
items.failure: An API returns accepted, the framework refetches, and the background job commits afterward.
items.agent: Establish exactly what an adapter response means on success, throw and timeout. If relevant writes remain live, a completion/polling mechanism is needed; a write footprint is insufficient.

items.claim: Result receipt, cache settlement and reconnect replay are different events.
items.current: The runtime settles after valid authority or reports read/transport failure; it does not automatically replay mutations.
items.failure: Treating handler success plus exhausted reads as a retryable write failure duplicates a committed action.
items.agent: Trace adapter outcome mapping and closure semantics. The runtime owns response validation and settlement; any future retry consumer needs its own admissibility claim.

items.claim: Configured runtime output validation.
items.current: Authoritative collection rows are validated in the client. Generated res.json is an identity function; no general server-side mutation-result/output schema enforcement is shown.
items.failure: A malformed or sensitive field crosses the wire before the client rejects the row.
items.agent: Add a schema/validator as ordinary code; inspect custom validators’ accepting paths. Evidence cannot substitute for running the validator before disclosure.

items.claim: Supported SQL compilation and explicit cross-tier conversion.
items.current: The compiler recognizes bounded query shapes and uses runtime row schemas. Unsupported result transforms do not acquire a general relational model.
items.failure: A custom bigint-to-number conversion maps two different IDs to the same browser key.
items.agent: Inspect a codec/transform for explicit identity, equality, ordering and membership laws over a stated domain. A proof/check does not implement missing query lowering.

items.claim: Validation/authorization precedes overridable persistence.
items.current: Mutation input and retained descriptors are admitted before the handler. Auth and persistence remain authored; custom validator purity is not automatically established.
items.failure: A persistence adapter returns a failure value the surrounding handler ignores, which becomes framework success.
items.agent: Inspect adapter participation and its actual success/error channel; verify accepting validators and whole-batch ordering when such a batch is authored.

items.claim: Checkpoint order, deletion retention and reconnect resync.
items.current: These replication obligations are outside the Endpoints refetch protocol; client sorting alone supplies none of them.
items.failure: A paged change reader uses a nonunique timestamp and permanently skips tied rows or deletes.
items.agent: For a future/existing sync adapter, inspect its cursor/deletion contract and run conformance checks. Standard SQL ordering belongs to compiler/catalog analysis, not an agent-only task.

items.claim: Backend event order and reset detection.
items.current: Query versions and client lifetimes reject some stale state. There is no backend reset protocol or general evidence-to-deployment binding.
items.failure: A remote database is replaced while local source hashes stay unchanged; an old contract is still treated as applicable.
items.agent: Bind a remote fact to an inspectable implementation/environment identity. A consumer must invalidate/recheck it on mismatch; evidence itself does not reset caches.

items.claim: Authorization at mount and privileged event boundaries.
items.current: Handlers can check each request. The compiler does not prove every application entry path is protected.
items.failure: A second endpoint invokes the same write helper without the authorization check in the first endpoint.
items.agent: Enumerate entry paths and inspect opaque checks against the application’s policy; repair uncovered paths as authored code.

items.claim: Code identity differs from mutable deployment names and environment identity.
items.current: Compiler versions include local source/schema evidence; a URL or package name is not bound to its current remote implementation/configuration.
items.failure: The API behind a stable URL gains a PG write without changing the endpoint source.
items.agent: Record exact inspectable remote revision/configuration and an invalidation condition. If identity cannot be established, the claim remains conditional or unknown.

items.claim: Post-call data and invalidated paths may exceed the returned result.
items.current: Retained collections are sent to the server and selected using footprints; handler result data is not treated as the full write set.
items.failure: Returning only the changed recipe misses shopping rows changed by an imported helper.
items.agent: Supply complete opaque read/write bounds for affected-query selection. The existing matcher can consume a union after an evidence adapter is implemented.

items.claim: Values stay separate from SQL/HTML code.
items.current: Supported Drizzle/SQL forms are analyzed; the footprint analyzer is not a general injection-safety checker or HTML escaper.
items.failure: A helper concatenates input into raw SQL while still touching only the expected table.
items.agent: Inspect raw helpers’ parameterization/escaping on every path. Use existing parameterized APIs or repair code where separation is absent; a correct footprint does not prove injection safety.

items.claim: Module encapsulation and schema agreement have an external-access boundary.
items.current: A build-time catalog snapshot is checked for format/hash. TS encapsulation does not restrict DB credentials or prove exclusive writers; unrelated writers are outside scope.
items.failure: A deployed migration changes table semantics after the analyzed snapshot was built.
items.agent: Bind analyzed schema and physical DB/environment to deployment. Do not require exclusive-writer proof for the user’s mutation-scoped coherence contract, or introduce per-request catalog scans.

items.claim: Generated route/endpoint identities do not collide.
items.current: Module/owner/name/ordinal identities and registry duplicate checks exist. This does not establish collision freedom for every unrelated app router/plugin.
items.failure: An opaque route plugin registers a path already owned by another handler.
items.agent: Inspect the plugin’s registrations if they are outside the route compiler. Visible registrations need a deterministic collision check, not certification prose.

items.claim: A decoder must establish the invariant assumed for client-supplied values.
items.current: Zod input parsing runs before the handler, but arbitrary refinements/decoders have only the guarantees their code enforces.
items.failure: A decoder casts a string to a validated tenant ID without checking its format or tenant membership.
items.agent: Inspect all accepted-value paths and downstream preconditions. Keep syntactic admission separate from actor authorization and from encode/decode round trips.

items.claim: Rollback-after-commit callbacks and irreversible post-SQL-commit hooks have distinct ordering.
items.current: No Endpoints foreign-effect transaction-hook protocol is present.
items.failure: An adapter makes an irreversible call in a callback that can still be followed by rollback.
items.agent: Inspect a particular existing hook runtime’s ordering and compensation behavior. New scheduling/compensation is implementation work, not a fact declaration.

items.claim: HTTP method/CSRF policy can depend on cookie reads and persistent effects.
items.current: Generated query and mutation server functions use POST. This alone proves neither CSRF protection nor read-only query behavior; Start’s full HTTP policy was not audited here.
items.failure: A cookie-authenticated request with a side effect is admitted without the required origin/token check.
items.agent: Trace hidden cookie reads/effects and actual HTTP protections if needed. The fact can drive linting; the app/server must enforce the chosen request policy.

items.claim: Escape hatches widen the code that an audit must cover.
items.current: Analyzed local helper files affect versions, but skipped imports and remote/configured hooks do not form a complete audited closure.
items.failure: A reviewed wrapper delegates to a newly configured hook outside the recorded dependency list.
items.agent: Enumerate reachable extension points and configuration, pin the evidence scope, and name unresolved paths. The evidence consumer must reject stale or incomplete claims for its required domain.

items.claim: Producer/consumer message compatibility includes runtime decoding.
items.current: Inputs and confirmation envelopes have runtime validation. There is no general actor/mailbox protocol system.
items.failure: A remote producer sends a syntactically valid success message whose payload violates the consumer’s expected domain.
items.agent: Inspect custom producer/decoder compatibility; standard endpoint schema compatibility is compiler/runtime work. Delivery and completion are separate obligations.

items.claim: Opaque predicates can prevent SQL lowering and move filter/limit execution.
items.current: Bounded shapes are modeled; unsupported transformed queries remain opaque rather than gaining an invented client predicate.
items.failure: Filtering after LIMIT produces different rows from filtering before LIMIT.
items.agent: Recover an opaque predicate’s meaning and preconditions. The compiler still needs a correct lowering rule; until then retain the full authored query/refetch path.

items.claim: Tier placement and opacity are different from source confidentiality.
items.current: Server handlers are extracted and server imports blocked in client loading; no Eliom client-fragment opacity/type calculus is implemented.
items.failure: A helper accesses browser APIs when invoked by server code, despite its source being excluded from the browser bundle.
items.agent: Inspect environmental requirements of unsupported helpers. Placement checks and bundle exclusion are compiler/build mechanisms; do not infer a cross-tier theorem for TS.

items.claim: Deferred-fragment order and primitive-definedness are premises of a restricted model.
items.current: No deferred-fragment scheduler or universal termination/type-preservation theorem applies to arbitrary endpoint JavaScript.
items.failure: A library throws for a nominally well-typed value, or a supposedly ordered effect runs asynchronously after return.
items.agent: Establish a bounded helper’s input domain, failure and ordering contract when needed. Historical theorem premises are not missing Endpoints features to implement wholesale.

items.claim: An ordinary validator can return accepted values and throw on rejection.
items.current: Zod parsing is installed; the implementation of a custom refinement/transform is not certified merely by its declared type.
items.failure: A custom validator accepts a negative quantity on one branch then returns a positive-quantity type.
items.agent: Inspect the installed validator’s accepting paths and transformations, or write a bounded exhaustive check. If it does not check the rule, fix the validator.

items.claim: Ordered parser composition determines final values and middleware observations.
items.current: The current boundary parses one generated envelope containing the declared input schema. It does not implement tRPC’s chained-input pipeline.
items.failure: A later transform overwrites a field already checked by an earlier validator.
items.agent: Trace actual parser order and final output through opaque schema helpers. For ordinary visible Zod composition this is reusable compiler analysis; preserve raw optimistic input separately.

items.claim: Output shape and output disclosure are separate guarantees.
items.current: Client row checks cannot prevent bytes already sent; generated handlers do not impose a server output whitelist.
items.failure: A query includes a secret field which the client schema strips or rejects only after delivery.
items.agent: Inspect whether an existing output parser actually strips/rejects forbidden fields before serialization, against an authored disclosure policy. Otherwise add the enforcement as code.

items.claim: Operation and metadata conditions determine which validation/auth checks run.
items.current: No Open RIA attribute pipeline exists. Endpoint checks are ordinary authored control flow, including deletes.
items.failure: A delete path assumes an entity validator will enforce ownership but never invokes it.
items.agent: Map each operation/entry path to the checks actually run. Do not import a source framework’s defaults as the intended Endpoints policy.

items.claim: Persistence error signaling must match the caller’s actual interpretation.
items.current: A resolved handler is encoded as success even if its returned application value denotes failure; thrown errors are separately encoded.
items.failure: An adapter returns false and its caller reports a successful save without examining it.
items.agent: Trace return values, thrown errors and side-channel error state through the real caller. Open RIA’s ignored Boolean is a source-specific example, not an Endpoints defect.

items.claim: Whole-batch admission can precede execution, without proving validation hooks pure.
items.current: Input and all retained query descriptors are checked before the write. A batch inside a handler has whatever validation order the author wrote.
items.failure: A handler writes item one before discovering item two is invalid.
items.agent: Inspect batch validation/control flow and custom validator effects. Use ordinary prevalidation/transactions where required; schema failure only proves the handler did not start.

items.claim: HTTP, durable, ephemeral and service effects are different domains.
items.current: Current dependency selection consumes PG relation sets, not a general effect system.
items.failure: A call makes no PG writes but charges money or changes an in-memory cache.
items.agent: Supply only the domains required by a named consumer. PG-write-empty can justify a refresh skip; it cannot justify retry, query determinism or confidentiality.

items.claim: Storage authority depends on environment and runtime configuration.
items.current: Physical module/relation binding and session scope are modeled locally; no Unison-style environment access system is provided.
items.failure: The same library/config key is routed to a different database or tenant.
items.agent: Trace the actual binding and authority context. Bind remote evidence to those dependencies without copying credentials into evidence records.

items.claim: Provisioning idempotence preserves resource identity across repeated deployment.
items.current: Resource provisioning is outside the endpoint query/mutation protocol.
items.failure: A repeated deployment helper creates a second database instead of reopening the first.
items.agent: If such a helper becomes relevant, inspect its lookup/create and concurrency contract. This is not evidence that user mutations are idempotent.

items.claim: Unexpected server errors are redacted.
items.current: refreshAfterMutation currently copies Error.message into the handler envelope; a framework-wide public/private error policy is absent on that path.
items.failure: A database exception includes SQL details or an internal URL and is sent to the browser.
items.agent: Inspect existing mapper paths and authored public error classes. A safe mapper must actually run; documenting the leak cannot prevent it.

items.claim: Query handlers are read-only as an application obligation.
items.current: Recognized direct query writes block a dependency proof, but that is not a general execution prohibition; imported calls may be skipped.
items.failure: A query helper updates last-seen state, and read retries repeat that write.
items.agent: Inspect hidden writes and other effects for the actual read/retry consumer. Normal SQL effects are compiler work; “query” as a declaration name is not proof.

items.claim: Intentional public error disclosure is conditional on status/type.
items.current: The handler error envelope has a string message, not a Wasp-style 4xx-only public error contract.
items.failure: An internal 500 is wrapped in a nominal public error and its details are exposed.
items.agent: Inspect all mapping conditions, not just the class name. Select and implement the app/framework error contract before certifying a mapper against it.

items.claim: Deterministic context supports query reuse and subscriptions.
items.current: The SQL analyzer marks recognized time/random functions as read uncertainty. Ordinary JS time, randomness and remote state are not controlled by a Convex-like executor.
items.failure: Date.now changes a query result without any table write that the dependency matcher can see.
items.agent: Describe relevant nondeterministic inputs and hidden reads. Evidence may disable a particular reuse optimization; it cannot freeze time or install subscriptions.

items.claim: Exported helpers are distinct from public endpoint registration.
items.current: The compiler creates handlers for query/mutation declarations, not every exported function; registry discovery has explicit module rules.
items.failure: A wrapper accidentally marks an internal administrative helper as a public endpoint.
items.agent: Inspect opaque registration plugins and reachability if used. Direct declarations are compiler-visible; endpoint reachability still does not imply authorization.

items.claim: Some clients preserve mutation issue order with a queue.
items.current: Endpoints deliberately dispatches overlapping actions without a mutation queue. Fresh settlement does not promise click-order execution.
items.failure: Set title A then B arrives as B then A; authority correctly ends at A.
items.agent: No certificate can add order. If an app operation requires it, express sequencing/preconditions in authored code; do not add an implicit global framework queue.

items.claim: Mutation consistency includes reads and deterministic decisions, not only atomic writes.
items.current: Authored PG transaction scope/isolation governs these properties; dependency extraction follows handles but does not prove isolation or conflict policy.
items.failure: Two transactions both read available stock and each decrements it without a suitable conditional update/lock.
items.agent: Inspect hidden read placement, participant handle and existing conflict checks. Atomicity alone is insufficient; business invariants and suitable SQL must be authored.

items.claim: Parallel actions require explicit sequencing for dependent work.
items.current: JavaScript awaits are preserved; the framework invokes concurrent actions without adding call order.
items.failure: A handler starts an async helper without awaiting it and returns before its writes.
items.agent: Lint visible unawaited calls; inspect an opaque helper’s promise-completion meaning. For dependent UI actions, use the returned transaction’s persistence completion where appropriate.

items.claim: Trusted caller identity and internal-only reachability are separate.
items.current: Generated requests carry scope, but that client-supplied value is not a trusted identity; handlers must derive/check the actual session.
items.failure: A public endpoint trusts scope=admin, or an internal helper loses caller context.
items.agent: Trace trusted session derivation and context forwarding through wrappers. Internal-only registration is a distinct routing property to check.

items.claim: Subtree data requirements compose before execution.
items.current: Retained endpoints are refreshed together, but component fragments are not compiled into a composed subtree query.
items.failure: A parent loads its data and only then discovers a child’s unrelated query, causing a waterfall.
items.agent: This needs a loading/composition mechanism if desired. An agent may refactor application loading code; evidence alone does not compose queries.

items.claim: Fetch provenance differs from coincidental cached-field availability.
items.current: Collections carry endpoint identity, not Relay fragment-spread witnesses for each component.
items.failure: A component appears to work only because an unrelated earlier screen fetched a field.
items.agent: A component contract or lint rule could expose accidental reliance. A new fragment witness API is not required for current collection coherence.

items.claim: Mutation response reads occur after processing and may follow declared fragments.
items.current: refreshAfterMutation awaits the handler before reading retained targets; no fragment response compiler or cross-query snapshot is implied.
items.failure: An opaque awaited API only queues a write; its response read is still too early.
items.agent: Establish helper closure/visibility before treating handler return as processing complete. No extra evidence is needed for the visible await-to-read ordering itself.

items.claim: Overlapping overlays, rollback and intervening authority need history checks.
items.current: Runtime overlap/topology handling and history regressions exist; arbitrary app action histories are not automatically certified.
items.failure: A second optimistic action relies on a row created by a first action that fails.
items.agent: Extend app generators to causal action histories and declared conflict semantics, exercising real actions and server paths. The independent framework oracle checks settlement, not app intent.

items.claim: Within-request operation order is distinct from transaction atomicity.
items.current: Authored await order is preserved; Promise.all remains concurrent and a transaction does not invent a requested order.
items.failure: An update races the insert it depends on inside a helper that launches both promises.
items.agent: Inspect helper scheduling/await behavior and preserve explicit dependencies in app code. Do not infer sequentiality merely from a shared request or transaction.

items.claim: Permission predicates must govern the executed write/read, not only a stale preflight.
items.current: Authored SQL can include predicates; the compiler does not insert or certify application policies.
items.failure: Ownership changes between an earlier permission check and an unrestricted update.
items.agent: Trace how opaque policy facts connect to the actual statement and transaction/isolation context. Repair authored predicates/locking when the connection is missing.

items.claim: Policies may constrain both old and proposed row state.
items.current: Input schemas and authored SQL can enforce this; there is no generated before/after permission system.
items.failure: A user owns a row before the update and changes its owner to an unauthorized account.
items.agent: Check accepting paths against explicit old-state and new-state rules. An agent cannot infer which ownership transfers the product intends to permit.

items.claim: Permission coverage includes every result object and every affected transaction object.
items.current: Endpoints validates row shape, not per-row permission coverage; bulk policy checks remain authored.
items.failure: A batch authorizes its first row but modifies additional unauthorized rows.
items.agent: Inspect loops, bulk WHERE predicates and helper-returned sets for complete policy coverage. Standard visible set logic belongs in reusable analysis.

items.claim: Transition and field policies must cover every submitted change.
items.current: Input parsing may strip unknown fields; valid schema fields are not automatically authorized fields.
items.failure: A valid title change is accompanied by a forbidden role change that passes an any-field check.
items.agent: Trace transformed input and enforce an authored all-fields rule against old/new values. A shape schema is not a permission policy.

items.claim: Schema creation has a distinct permission boundary.
items.current: Client requests do not carry arbitrary SQL/schema changes in this protocol; migration/admin endpoints, if authored, still need policy.
items.failure: An administrative helper permits adding a protected attribute even though ordinary row writes are denied.
items.agent: Inspect relevant admin paths only when present. Do not add schema-edit permissions to ordinary data endpoints solely for parity with a schemaless source.

items.claim: Idempotence differs from effect-freedom and arbitrary function execution.
items.current: Read paths retry; mutations are not automatically retried. SQL UPDATE does not by itself prove idempotence because expressions/triggers may differ.
items.failure: Repeating “increment count” changes state twice even though the endpoint is named setCount.
items.agent: Establish a precise repeat-execution law over relevant state and effects, or an existing deduplication contract. A future replay consumer must require that law, not a verb/name.

items.claim: Operations target stable entity identity, not current array position.
items.current: Endpoint rows use id keys and queries have canonical instance identities. Application code can still choose the wrong row from a list index.
items.failure: A user selects item at index 2; reordering occurs; index 2 now names another item.
items.agent: Trace ID selection and custom key/codec stability through helper boundaries. Framework keying is present; application selection semantics are separate.

items.claim: Stale response rejection needs trustworthy version provenance and comparison scope.
items.current: Epoch/topology checks and fresh reads handle overlapping local operations; this is not a global timestamp/LSN ordering protocol.
items.failure: A numerically larger timestamp from another clock is accepted as newer authority.
items.agent: For future manifests, establish version source and comparability domain. Evidence cannot implement ordering; LSN/version optimization remains deferred.

items.claim: Different users must not share a browser data cache.
items.current: EndpointRuntime binds one scope to one DbClient and rejects scope changes; applications must create/clean up the appropriate client lifetime.
items.failure: Logout switches a UI identity but leaves another user’s retained client accessible.
items.agent: Trace app session-to-client ownership and cleanup, including asynchronous callbacks. Scope partitioning does not prove server authorization.

items.claim: Acknowledgment must include acknowledged effects; replay engines also preserve per-client order.
items.current: Inline response admission/refresh settles local actions, without durable sequence acknowledgments or replay order.
items.failure: An adapter acknowledges a mutation that is still queued, and the client drops its overlay.
items.agent: Inspect acknowledgment/visibility coupling in an existing adapter. Queue ordering and replay state need machinery if later selected.

items.claim: Conflict behavior depends on application semantics and current authority.
items.current: The server executes authored conflict logic; the framework does not choose reservation/merge policy.
items.failure: Optimism reserves a now-unavailable item; a server rejection is expected, not an oracle failure by itself.
items.agent: Supply concurrent-state generators and explicit permitted outcomes. Check authored policy separately from the framework’s rollback/settlement law.

items.claim: Failed upload acknowledgment may mean applied, discarded or durably queued.
items.current: No FIFO upload queue/checkpoint engine exists. Endpoints reports read/transport failures rather than promising queue progress.
items.failure: A permanent rejection is repeatedly retried and prevents later queued changes from advancing.
items.agent: For an adapter, trace every terminal outcome and its actual liveness behavior. Choosing discard versus retry is app policy; a successful HTTP response alone proves none of them.

items.claim: Write identity differs from row identity, especially when confirming deletes.
items.current: RPC/transaction association correlates Endpoints calls; it does not use Electric’s operation-tagged replication matching.
items.failure: Two updates to the same row are confused by an adapter that matches only row ID.
items.agent: Trace an existing write ID end to end, including delete handling and reuse. Do not infer per-operation confirmation from entity identity alone.

items.claim: Causal rollback is different from discarding all pending work.
items.current: Transactions isolate overlays and fresh reads settle overlaps. There is no general application dependency graph or durable replay of dependent writes.
items.failure: Create fails; a pending edit of that new row is still treated as independently valid.
items.agent: Identify causal dependencies in authored actions and test failure histories. Automatic selective replay/cancellation would require a separate protocol.

items.claim: Optimistic state has an ownership scope and lifetime.
items.current: Collections/actions bind to DbClient, not a component-local array. Cleanup retires collections; pending state is not durable across reload.
items.failure: Two UI roots accidentally use different clients for one intended session and display different guesses.
items.agent: Inspect client sharing, cleanup and intended lifetime in the application. Persistence/offline semantics require additional mechanisms if desired.

items.claim: Server-only execution is weaker than excluding server source from client delivery.
items.current: The compiler extracts handlers; load guards and sourcemap handling exclude declared server modules. Built-artifact oracle checks exist for generated cases.
items.failure: A runtime isServer conditional leaves a secret literal inside a delivered client module.
items.agent: For unrecognized dependencies, inspect environmental/source classification and extend deterministic build checks. Existing bundle checks are framework evidence, not an app-specific certificate.

items.claim: Remote error redaction differs from local server error detail.
items.current: Mutation Error.message is passed into the client envelope; no distinct internal/public error mapper is enforced there.
items.failure: An internal exception suitable for server logs exposes account or connection details to the client.
items.agent: Inspect custom mapper and logging paths against an authored disclosure contract; add the mapper where absent. This overlaps Q01, not a second independent defect.

items.claim: Replay can be prevented or deduplicated with a real call-ID contract.
items.current: No automatic mutation retry is installed; there is no general server deduplication store.
items.failure: After losing a success response, an app resubmits the mutation and duplicates its effect.
items.agent: Inspect existing atomic deduplication, key scope, result reuse, retention and concurrent duplicate handling. A token parameter without that machinery is insufficient.

items.claim: Conflict detection compares assumed master state with actual state.
items.current: The endpoint protocol has no automatic compare-and-swap or master-wins conflict algorithm; SQL can express authored preconditions.
items.failure: An update based on version 4 overwrites a row already at version 5.
items.agent: Inspect the adapter’s compare/write atomicity and returned conflict state. If absent, implement the intended conditional SQL/policy; do not import master-wins by default.

items.claim: Checkpoint timestamps must come from a trusted ordering authority.
items.current: Current endpoint settlement does not trust client timestamps as sync checkpoints.
items.failure: A future incremental reader accepts a client-supplied future time and skips subsequent writes.
items.agent: Trace timestamp assignment and ordering domain if an adapter introduces checkpoints. Standard SQL generation/ordering is compiler work; no checkpoint feature is currently needed.

items.claim: Repeated sync modifiers need an effect-free contract.
items.current: There is no push/pull modifier pipeline. Similar obligations matter for any installed retried read/transform helper.
items.failure: A modifier charges or writes an audit record each time the same batch is retried.
items.agent: Inspect exact modifier effects across hooks and errors. The effect domain required for replay is broader than the table set required for invalidation.

items.claim: Lost responses can duplicate already-completed processing.
items.current: Unknown mutation outcomes are not automatically retried; user/app resubmission remains possible.
items.failure: The server commits, the connection drops, and a second request repeats the external effect.
items.agent: Establish existing deduplication/idempotence if replay is desired. A green normal-response test or read-only PG footprint cannot establish this.

items.claim: Actor identity comes from trusted session context, not request arguments.
items.current: The generated envelope validates scope as a nonempty string, which is not authentication. Authored handlers must validate it against server context.
items.failure: A user changes the scope field to another user ID in a forged request.
items.agent: Trace session derivation and every privileged use, including helper forwarding. An agent can repair the handler; the compiler must not insert auth behavior.

items.claim: Validation rejection, handler failure and transport failure have different semantics.
items.current: InvalidInputError, not-started, handler outcome and read-error envelopes exist. Unknown transport outcomes remain distinct; the system is not Zero’s skip/retry protocol.
items.failure: A broad catch converts a timeout after commit into “nothing happened,” permitting unsafe retry.
items.agent: Inspect opaque adapter error mapping and whether writes may continue. Runtime validation/classification stays framework work; do not conflate failure with rollback.

items.claim: Existing/missing rows and null/undefined have operation-specific semantics.
items.current: DB actions and authored PG SQL decide behavior; Endpoints does not impose Zero’s successful-no-op rules.
items.failure: Optimistic update of a missing row throws while authored SQL updates zero rows successfully, or undefined is confused with NULL.
items.agent: Generate these states and compare according to the actual app/adapter contract. Inspect opaque write-helper defaults; do not declare source-framework parity as the expected oracle.

items.claim: Identity mismatch needs a defined consumer response.
items.current: Stale query versions reject with reload guidance, scope changes reject, and dev source changes trigger reload. General evidence mismatch behavior is not implemented.
items.failure: An evidence checker detects a stale remote contract but the matcher still uses its old write bound.
items.agent: Bind the configured stop/refetch/recheck behavior as well as identity. Detection alone supplies no safety unless the consumer stops relying on the invalid claim.

items.claim: The inspected LiveStore docs explicitly lack merge-conflict handling.
items.current: This is a source limitation, not a positive guarantee missing from Endpoints.
items.failure: A comparison table credits a conflict guarantee the inspected source explicitly says is unfinished.
items.agent: No certification task follows. Preserve the negative source claim; do not turn it into an implementation requirement or evidence opportunity.

items.claim: Navigation and component/event paths can bypass the first middleware check.
items.current: Endpoint handlers are explicit server entry points, but application routes/actions outside them were not exhaustively audited here.
items.failure: A route checked during initial load later exposes a privileged action through a separate handler without rechecking.
items.agent: Enumerate actual entry paths and their context/checks, including opaque framework wrappers. This is code-path analysis plus authored policy, not automatic auth rewriting.

items.claim: Revocation requires a response for already-active sessions/connections.
items.current: Scope changes are rejected when resolved; that does not autonomously learn server revocation or erase all active browser data.
items.failure: A revoked user keeps an open tab showing cached data and attempts further actions.
items.agent: Trace the app’s request checks, logout/client cleanup and any event-driven revocation. Live socket disconnect/sync is outside this transport; future requests still need authored checks.

items.claim: Firestore read-before-write and offline rules are operation-specific.
items.current: Endpoints uses PG and has no Firestore offline transaction/batch API. These restrictions do not transfer to arbitrary PG transactions.
items.failure: An audit wrongly rejects valid PG read-after-write code because it imports Firestore’s rule.
items.agent: Only inspect these rules for an actual Firestore adapter. Preserve the source boundary rather than adding unrelated Endpoints restrictions.

items.claim: Atomic writes can still violate a cross-row business invariant.
items.current: A PG transaction can supply atomicity; correctness of totals, balances or paired updates remains authored SQL/constraints/policy.
items.failure: Both debit and credit commit together, but their amounts differ.
items.agent: Given an explicit invariant, inspect hidden helper semantics or build an independent domain oracle. Compiler/catalog checks can recognize existing constraints; neither infers business intent.
